text:
anya: bringing up polaris-7b int4 on our infra, quick eval shows a 3.2% accuracy/regression on LlamaBench. suspect rotary freq/head-scaling mismatch and maybe an EOS/token-id remap problem.

devon: can you paste the tokenizer config you used? did the converter apply a vocab offset or remap?

anya: converter used the upstream mapping with no explicit offset. snippet from conversion log: 
```
model.vocab_offset = 0
tokenizer.eos_token_id = 50256
```

marta: whoa 50256 looks GPT2-like. polaris checkpoints we've seen set eos=1. an off-by-one in the mapping would explain weird completions. try rerunning with `vocab_offset=1`. :thinking:

keith: also check rotary/freq params — some of these newer models used nonstandard base/freq scaling per-head. if our runtime assumes base=10000 but model pretrain used 10000*1.2 you'll get phase drift across heads. can you run a rotary sanity check? e.g. `python -m tests.rotary_check --seq 1024 --headwise`.

anya: ran vocab_offset=1, quick smoke reduces ppl delta from +3.2% -> +0.8% on the small suite. still seeing a few hallucinations in completions. logs: 
```
[eval] seed=42, ppl=12.4 -> 12.1
[diff] topk mismatches: 14/100 prompts
```

devon: topk mismatches down to 14/100 is promising. could be pad token / kv-cache indexing aliasing too. did you set pad_token_id explicitly when building tokenizer?

anya: pad_token_id was unset in the conversion. set pad_token_id=0 and re-ran: mismatches -> 4/100. so both vocab remap and pad aliasing were contributing.

marta: good catch. we should add a conversion option to assert eos/pad invariants and emit warnings. also add a tiny unit that compares tokenization between source and converted tokenizer for 100 random sentences.

keith: for the remaining 4/100 mismatches, instrument the attention keys/queries at step=1 to see if rotary phase differs headwise. if headwise scaling is off you'll see steady phase offsets that alter attention.

anya: I dumped head0/key vectors from both runtimes and saw a small rotation-phase offset in higher-frequency heads. example diff (normed): 0.06 mean phase error on heads 8-11.

devon: that matches my suspicion — some models apply headwise freq multipliers or tuned rotary_scale. quick mitigation: runtime flag `--rotary-scale=1.0|auto|headwise-map` to force compatibility or to read mapping from model metadata. we should prefer metadata autotune.

marta: agree. I'll add a check in onboarding CI to validate `rotary_scale` by measuring cosine similarity between original and loaded head embeddings for a short prompt. fail CI if similarity < 0.98 unless explicit opt-in.

keith: also consider adding a conversion patch that writes a small `compat.json` alongside the weights with fields: eos_token_id, pad_token_id, vocab_offset, rotary_base, rotary_scale_hint. That way runtime can auto-apply fixes.

eval-bot: scheduled job polaris-7b-int4-compat-check at 3950012400. will post full metrics here when done.

anya: thanks — I'll push a patch to the converter to allow explicit mapping table and set pad/eos defaults and add the compat.json. also adding note to model card about tokenizer semantics. :pray:

keith: pinging @marta to review converter PR when ready.

marta: will review. if we still see headwise drift after the mapping fix, try forcing `rotary_scale=1.0` in runtime as a short-term fallback and open an R&D ticket to measure perf/quality tradeoffs.

devon: can you paste the single failing prompt that still hallucinates? that'll help isolate if it's a tokenization mismatch vs model weight issue.

anya: I'll paste the prompt + model output once CI finishes — short factual Q/A that returns an incorrect year; looks like off-by-one in date tokens.

keith: ok, let's reconvene once the CI/eval run posts results. thanks everyone for quick triage.
